LESSON: REARING SMALL DOMESTIC ANIMALS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESSES Strand Sub strand Specific learning outcomes Suggested
Topic 2.1: Rearing Small Domestic Animals
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rearing Small Domestic Animals, part of FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESSES Strand Sub strand Specific learning outcomes Suggested in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six AGRICULTURE.

Key inquiry question: How does rearing of animals contribute to food production?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rearing Small Domestic Animals together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Integrity: fairness in allocation of resources and tasks in the project for rearing small domestic animals.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Animal welfare in the handling and caring for small domestic animals.

Link to other subjects:

Learners relate rearing of small domestic animals to knowledge of farming as a socio-economic activity learnt in social

studies.

• Captioned video clips

• Small domestic animals such as rabbits

• Water for sanitation
